page: Amazon Web Services t3.2xlarge is a burstable performance instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an x86_64 architecture utilizing an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile due to the burstable CPU allocation model. Under stress-ng, single-core CPU performance is categorized as weak, while multi-core performance reaches average levels. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes consistently rank in the average tier. However, single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show weak to poor performance. Geekbench scores also reflect this trend, with single-core metrics in the bottom 10% and multi-core metrics in the bottom 25%, though software compilation with Clang achieves average marks.

The burstable CPU allocation makes the t3.2xlarge a cost-effective choice for workloads with variable resource demands. It is highly efficient for applications that experience periodic spikes in activity rather than sustained high CPU utilization, as continuous heavy compute will deplete CPU credits. This profile is well-suited for development environments, code compilation, low-to-medium traffic web servers, and microservices that benefit from a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio without requiring dedicated, non-burstable hardware.
